blogArticles.title: Why Notebook Handwriting and Independent Attempts Tell Us More Than Marks Alone
blogArticles.author: Dr. Meenakshi Deswal
blogArticles.excerpt: How a single 30-second whole-class notebook check generates structured evidence for Organising Ability, Power of Expression, and Determination without extra teacher paperwork.
blogArticles.body: In Indian classrooms, teachers already inspect dozens of notebooks every afternoon. Yet those observations usually stay inked on paper and are forgotten before parent-teacher meetings. In Virat Student 360°, recording Readability and Work Quality (A: independent and correct, B: independent attempt with mistakes, C: requires review) links everyday classroom effort directly to Planning, Organising, and Dynamic Qualities—while ensuring an honest mistake in an independent attempt is valued as Determination rather than penalised.

blogArticles.title: Choosing Class 11 Streams in Haryana & North India: Avoiding Peer-Pressure Decisions
blogArticles.author: Dr. Sunita Gill
blogArticles.excerpt: A practical framework combining CUET subject eligibility, student interest consistency, and counsellor review for Class 10 students and parents.
blogArticles.body: Every April, thousands of Class 10 students select Science, Commerce, or Humanities based on hearsay rather than aptitude and university eligibility. Our advisory framework pairs evidence of sustained reasoning and curiosity with current CUET, JEE, NEET, CLAT, and NDA pathways—always reviewed by a human career counsellor before finalising recommendations.

blogArticles.title: Fair Assessment Without Labels: Moving Beyond "Active vs Passive" Student Tags
blogArticles.author: Anil Kumar Hooda
blogArticles.excerpt: Why quiet, reflective learners thrive when schools evaluate written curiosity, mistake recovery, and missing-evidence safeguards fairly.
blogArticles.body: Labelling a quiet student as "passive" can follow them across academic years and undermine confidence. Virat Student 360° prohibits permanent labels, never treats missing evidence as zero, and separates attendance context from personality indicators.

overview.summary: Design, build, test, and maintain software platforms, web/mobile applications, and responsible AI-assisted digital systems across healthcare, education, finance, and public infrastructure.
overview.corePurpose: Translate complex real-world human and organizational problems into reliable, scalable digital solutions.

milestones: Build deep mastery in NCERT Mathematics & Physics
Learn one programming language (Python or JavaScript)
Core CS fundamentals (DSA, OS, DBMS, Networks)
2–3 real deployed software projects
Summer industry internship
Production code reviews & system ownership
Optional M.Tech / MS via GATE for deep R&D

aptitudeProfile.iqFocus: Strong abstract reasoning, mathematical logic, and structured problem decomposition.
aptitudeProfile.eqFocus: Empathy for end-users, constructive receptiveness during peer code reviews, and calm collaboration.
aptitudeProfile.aqFocus: High resilience when debugging unfamiliar failures and adapting to rapidly evolving tools.
aptitudeProfile.cqFocus: Creative system architecture, clean UX thinking, and original ways to automate manual bottlenecks.

speechExercises.title: Stage 6: Sentence Practice — /r/ (English)
speechExercises.learningObjective: Reading sentences, picture description, and structured dialogue for target /r/ in English.
speechExercises.therapistInstructions: Model structured sentence production and picture description with /r/. Note carryover accuracy vs. word-level baseline.
speechExercises.studentInstructions: Read or repeat each sentence aloud, or describe the matching picture in your own words.
practiceItems: Rohan saw a red robin near the river.
The rabbit ate a crunchy carrot in the garden.
We drew a bright star on the green chart.

speechExercises.title: Stage 4: Word Practice — English /r/ Picture Naming
speechExercises.learningObjective: Stabilise clear initial and medial English /r/ in familiar everyday words with relaxed pacing.
speechExercises.therapistInstructions: Use picture cards for initial (/r/: rain, red, rabbit, river) and medial (carrot, parrot, orange). Record word-level accuracy without rushing.
speechExercises.studentInstructions: Name each picture clearly and enjoy spotting your /r/ sound in the word! Take a tiny smile break after every 5 words.
practiceItems: Initial /r/: rain, red, rabbit, river, ribbon
Pick 2 favourite words and draw a quick doodle for them
speechExercises.therapistFeedback: Abhiraj reached 78% accuracy on initial /r/ words in session 4 — ready for relaxed home games.

speechExercises.title: Stage 5: Functional Phrase Bridge — English /r/
speechExercises.learningObjective: Carry over clear /r/ into natural 2–3 word functional phrases.
speechExercises.therapistInstructions: Model natural conversational stress; reinforce self-monitoring gently.
speechExercises.studentInstructions: Say each mini-phrase smoothly like a story narrator — no hurry at all!
speechExercises.therapistFeedback: Keep home sessions joyful and stop early if tired.

clinicalReports.title: Speech & Language Assessment Report — Abhiraj
clinicalReports.languageAndSpeechProfile: Bilingual Hindi/English speaker with strong receptive and expressive language in both languages. Hindi tap र intact; targeted English prevocalic /r/ substitution (/w/ for /r/) in initial and medial positions. Regional Indian English accent differences respected and excluded from error count.
clinicalReports.clinicalAssessmentFindings: Stimulable for English /r/ with visual placement cues; bilateral hearing cleared by Consulting Audiologist.
recommendations: Twice-weekly 30-minute SLP sessions progressing across Stages 4–6.
Relaxed 10-minute home picture/phrase games 4–5 times weekly.
Natural classroom recasting without public correction.
clinicalReports.parentFriendlySummary: Abhiraj has strong language skills in both Hindi and English and hears clearly. Together we are practising clearer English /r/ sounds through short, playful word and phrase games.
clinicalReports.teacherAuthorizedSummary: Continue encouraging oral participation; model target English /r/ words warmly in conversation rather than correcting in front of classmates.

clinicalReports.title: Monthly Speech Therapy Progress Report — Abhiraj
clinicalReports.baselineAndProgressSummary: English /r/ word-level accuracy progressed steadily from 62% (Oct 18 baseline) to 82% in functional 2-word phrases (Nov 18) with minimal cueing. Student comfort and willingness to volunteer in class remain high (5/5).
recommendations: Transition toward Stage 6 structured sentences over the next 3 weeks.
Maintain joyful 10-minute home practice games without pressure.
Scheduled SLP reassessment on 18 Dec 2026.
clinicalReports.parentFriendlySummary: Abhiraj has made steady, confident progress on English /r/ words and phrases this month! Home play sessions are making a big difference.
clinicalReports.teacherAuthorizedSummary: Student is ready for positive encouragement during short partner reading in English.

clinicalReports.title: Developmental Screening Workflow Summary — Jasika
clinicalReports.screeningFindings: Non-diagnostic screening workflow initiated following teacher and parent input regarding written task chunking and evening sleep schedule. Strong oral reasoning and peer warmth observed.
recommendations: Complete 2-week home sleep & routine log.
Trial Special Educator 3-step visual checklists in class for 6 weeks.
Review cross-setting functioning before determining whether any formal clinical evaluation is needed.
clinicalReports.parentFriendlySummary: This is a supportive check-in summary, not a clinical diagnosis. We are partnering with you on sleep routines and step-by-step study checklists to help written work match strong oral understanding.
clinicalReports.teacherAuthorizedSummary: Provide 3-step written task checklists and short movement transitions between long writing blocks.

chapterBlueprints.subject: Science
chapterBlueprints.overview: Explores how green plants synthesize food via photosynthesis, how stomata and chlorophyll work, and how parasitic, insectivorous, and saprotrophic plants obtain nutrients.

concepts.title: Autotrophic vs Heterotrophic Nutrition
concepts.explanation: Autotrophs like green plants prepare their own food from simple inorganic substances (CO2 and water), while heterotrophs depend directly or indirectly on plants.
practicalApplications: Recognizing producers vs consumers in school gardens
learningObjectives: Differentiate autotrophs and heterotrophs with local examples
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Science · Ch. 1: Nutrition in Plants

concepts.title: Photosynthesis Process & Equation
concepts.explanation: In the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll, leaves convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose (starch) and release oxygen.
practicalApplications: Testing leaf starch with iodine solution in the school lab
learningObjectives: Explain inputs, energy source, and outputs of photosynthesis
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Science · Ch. 1: Nutrition in Plants

concepts.title: Stomata, Guard Cells & Chloroplasts
concepts.explanation: Tiny pores called stomata on leaf surfaces are guarded by bean-shaped guard cells that regulate CO2 intake and oxygen/water vapour release.
practicalApplications: Why plants wilt in extreme heat when stomata close
learningObjectives: Label guard cells, stomatal pore, and chloroplasts accurately
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Science · Ch. 1: Nutrition in Plants

concepts.title: Parasitic, Insectivorous & Saprotrophic Plants
concepts.explanation: Cuscuta absorbs nutrients as a parasite, Pitcher plants trap insects for nitrogen, and fungi like mushrooms digest dead organic matter saprotrophically.
practicalApplications: Observing bread mould and nitrogen-poor wetland adaptations
learningObjectives: Classify non-green nutrition strategies in plants
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Science · Ch. 1: Nutrition in Plants

concepts.title: Rhizobium & Soil Nutrient Replenishment
concepts.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria live inside legume root nodules, converting atmospheric nitrogen into soluble forms in exchange for food and shelter (symbiosis).
practicalApplications: Crop rotation by farmers using pulses to restore soil fertility
learningObjectives: Explain symbiotic nitrogen fixation in agricultural fields
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Science · Ch. 1: Nutrition in Plants

suggestedExperiments: Iodine Starch Test on Sunlight vs Dark Leaf

chapterBlueprints.subject: Science
chapterBlueprints.chapterTitle: Nutrition in Animals — Human Digestive System
chapterBlueprints.overview: Follows the complete path of food through the human alimentary canal—from ingestion and salivary amylase in the mouth to peristalsis, stomach enzymes, small intestine villi absorption, and egestion.

concepts.title: Mechanical & Salivary Digestion in the Mouth
concepts.explanation: Teeth chew food mechanically while salivary glands secrete saliva containing amylase to break starch into simple sugars.
diagramsAndProcesses: Types of teeth & salivary gland diagram
practicalApplications: Why chewing rice longer makes it taste subtly sweet
learningObjectives: Explain mechanical vs chemical digestion starting in the mouth
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Science · Ch. 2: Nutrition in Animals

concepts.title: Oesophagus Peristalsis & Stomach Juices
concepts.explanation: Wave-like muscular contractions (peristalsis) move food down the oesophagus into the stomach where mucus, HCl, and digestive enzymes break down proteins.
practicalApplications: Understanding why acid reflux occurs and how mucus protects stomach walls
learningObjectives: Describe the triple role of mucus, HCl, and digestive juices in the stomach
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Science · Ch. 2: Nutrition in Animals

concepts.title: Small Intestine Villi Absorption & Large Intestine
concepts.explanation: Bile from the liver emulsifies fats, pancreatic juices complete digestion, finger-like villi absorb nutrients into blood, and the large intestine reabsorbs water before egestion.
practicalApplications: How surface area multiplication speeds nutrient absorption
learningObjectives: Trace nutrient absorption in villi and water absorption in the large intestine
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Science · Ch. 2: Nutrition in Animals

chapterBlueprints.subject: Mathematics
chapterBlueprints.overview: Connects visual fraction ratios, 2D perimeter/area formulas, and 3D cuboid & cylinder surface area and volume through interactive geometric modeling.

concepts.title: Visual Fractions & Equivalent Ratios
concepts.explanation: Multiplying or dividing both numerator and denominator by the same non-zero integer preserves the proportional fraction of a whole.
practicalApplications: Scaling recipes, architectural blueprints, and map scales
learningObjectives: Construct and compare equivalent fractions visually
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 8 Mathematics · Ch. 9: Mensuration

concepts.title: Cuboid & Cylinder Surface Area vs Volume
concepts.explanation: Surface area measures the outer wrapping in square units (e.g. 2(lb+bh+hl)), while volume measures inner 3D capacity in cubic units (l × b × h).
practicalApplications: Calculating water tank capacity and gift-box paper needed
learningObjectives: Distinguish total surface area from volume when dimensions change
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 8 Mathematics · Ch. 9: Mensuration

suggestedExperiments: Doubling Side Length Effect on Volume

chapterBlueprints.subject: Science
chapterBlueprints.overview: Explains how solar heating drives continuous water circulation through evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, and groundwater recharge.

concepts.title: Evaporation, Condensation & Precipitation Cycle
concepts.explanation: Solar heat evaporates surface water into vapour which rises, cools, condenses into droplets forming clouds, and returns to Earth as rain or snow.
practicalApplications: Rainwater harvesting and drought conservation
learningObjectives: Trace how temperature controls evaporation and rainfall rate
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 6 Science · Ch. 14: Water

chapterBlueprints.subject: Science
chapterBlueprints.overview: Demonstrates closed circuits, conductors vs insulators, voltage, resistance, and electric current flow using live virtual laboratory simulations.

concepts.title: Voltage, Resistance & Current Flow (I = V / R)
concepts.explanation: Increasing battery voltage increases current flow in a closed circuit, while increasing electrical resistance reduces current and dims the lamp.
practicalApplications: Household fuses, LED brightness control, and circuit safety
learningObjectives: Predict current and bulb brightness when voltage or resistance changes
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 8 Science · Ch. 12: Electricity

assessmentRecommendations: Ohm’s Law calculation & circuit fault identification

chapterBlueprints.subject: Social Science
chapterBlueprints.chapterTitle: Our Changing Earth — Volcanoes & Plate Tectonics
chapterBlueprints.overview: Investigates lithospheric plates, endogenic forces, magma chambers, volcanic eruptions, seismic focus/epicentre, and disaster preparedness.

concepts.title: Tectonic Plates, Magma Vent & Seismic Waves
concepts.explanation: Slow motion of lithospheric plates builds pressure in Earth’s mantle; sudden release causes earthquakes from a focus, while molten magma erupts through volcanic vents.
prerequisites: Layers of the Earth (Crust, Mantle, Core)
practicalApplications: Seismic safety drills and Ring of Fire geography
learningObjectives: Differentiate focus vs epicentre and magma vs lava
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Social Science · Ch. 3: Our Changing Earth

chapterBlueprints.subject: English
chapterBlueprints.overview: Builds practical grammar confidence through visual tense timelines, error-spotting challenges, vocabulary word search, and real-world polite dialogue role-play.

concepts.title: Subject-Verb Agreement & Tense Timeline
concepts.explanation: Verbs shift form to match both the subject (singular/plural) and the point on the time line (past, present, or future).
practicalApplications: Writing clear reports, letters, and confident spoken dialogues
learningObjectives: Identify tense shifts and fix subject-verb agreement errors
concepts.sourceReference: HBSE Class 6 English Grammar · Ch. 4

suggestedSimulations: Interactive Library & Science Fair Dialogue Role-Play

interactiveGames.subject: Science
interactiveGames.learningObjective: Classify organisms accurately by their mode of nutrition.
interactiveGames.title: Plant Nutrition Mode Sorter
interactiveGames.instructions: Sort each organism into its correct mode of nutrition bin: Autotroph, Parasite/Insectivore, or Saprotroph.

items.explanation: Contains chlorophyll and prepares its own food via photosynthesis.
Lacks chlorophyll and draws ready-made food from a host plant.
Secretes digestive juices onto dead organic matter and absorbs nutrients.
Traps insects in a modified leaf pitcher to obtain nitrogen.
Grows on stale moist bread by digesting decaying nutrients.
Green algae perform photosynthesis in sunlit water.

interactiveGames.answerKeySummary: Autotroph: Neem, Algae | Parasite/Insectivore: Cuscuta, Pitcher Plant | Saprotroph: Mushroom, Bread Mould

interactiveGames.subject: Science
interactiveGames.learningObjective: Arrange the step-by-step sequence of photosynthesis in exact biological order.
interactiveGames.title: Photosynthesis Step Sequence Builder
interactiveGames.instructions: Tap the 5 stages in exact order from raw material intake to starch storage and oxygen release.

items.prompt: Roots absorb water & minerals from soil and transport them via xylem.
items.explanation: Water travels upward through root hairs and xylem vessels to the leaves.

items.prompt: Stomata open to take in carbon dioxide (CO₂) from the surrounding air.
items.explanation: Guard cells open stomatal pores to allow CO₂ diffusion into leaf cells.

items.prompt: Chlorophyll inside chloroplasts captures sunlight energy.
items.explanation: Green chlorophyll pigment traps solar energy needed to drive the chemical reaction.

items.prompt: Light energy converts CO₂ and water into glucose (carbohydrate).
items.explanation: Glucose is synthesized and later stored as starch in leaves and fruits.

experientialSimulations.subject: Science
experientialSimulations.chapterTitle: Nutrition in Animals — Human Digestive System
experientialSimulations.learningObjective: Trace a real food particle through all stages of human digestion with mechanical, enzymatic, and absorption processes.
experientialSimulations.title: Human Digestive System: Live Food-Particle Journey
experientialSimulations.subtitle: Select a food particle (Apple, Roti, or Cheese) and guide it through all 7 animated stages from Mouth to Elimination.
experientialSimulations.instructions: Pick a food particle, click Play Journey or step through each stage, listen to narration, inspect organ labels, and answer stage checkpoints.

stages.title: Ingestion & Mechanical Chewing (Mouth)
stages.narration: Digestion begins right in the mouth! Teeth grind food mechanically into a soft bolus while salivary glands mix in saliva.
stages.explanation: Teeth increase surface area by chewing, while salivary amylase starts converting complex starch into simple sugars.
stages.checkpointQuestion: Which nutrient begins chemical digestion right inside the mouth due to saliva?
stages.checkpointExplanation: Salivary amylase breaks starch into simple maltose sugars while chewing.

stages.title: Peristalsis Through the Oesophagus
stages.narration: The chewed bolus enters the food pipe, or oesophagus. Rhythmic muscular waves called peristalsis gently push it downward to the stomach.
stages.explanation: Peristaltic waves push food downward even against gravity; no major chemical digestion occurs here.
stages.checkpointQuestion: What pushes food smoothly down the oesophagus into the stomach?
stages.checkpointExplanation: Rhythmic muscular contractions called peristalsis move food down the alimentary canal.

stages.title: Acid Bath & Churning in the Stomach
stages.narration: Inside the J-shaped stomach, churning mixes food with hydrochloric acid, protective mucus, and protein-digesting enzymes.
stages.explanation: HCl kills harmful bacteria and activates digestive juices to break proteins into simpler compounds, while mucus shields the stomach lining.
stages.checkpointQuestion: What protects the inner lining of the stomach from its own hydrochloric acid?
stages.checkpointExplanation: The stomach secretes mucus that coats and shields its inner wall from acidic damage.

stages.title: Liver Bile & Pancreatic Juices
stages.narration: As chyme enters the upper small intestine, the liver contributes bile stored in the gall bladder and the pancreas adds powerful multi-nutrient enzymes.
stages.explanation: Bile breaks large fat globules into tiny droplets (emulsification), while pancreatic juice acts on carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.
stages.checkpointQuestion: Where is bile produced, and which nutrient does it help break down?
checkpointOptions: Produced in Liver; helps digest Fats
Produced in Large Intestine; absorbs Water
stages.checkpointExplanation: The liver produces bile (stored in the gall bladder) which emulsifies fats.

stages.title: Nutrient Absorption in Small Intestine Villi
stages.narration: Inside the coiled 7.5-metre small intestine, thousands of microscopic finger-like villi absorb glucose, amino acids, and fatty acids directly into the bloodstream!
stages.explanation: Villi multiply internal surface area and contain dense blood capillaries that carry absorbed nutrients to every cell for assimilation.
stages.checkpointQuestion: Why does the inner wall of the small intestine have thousands of finger-like villi?
checkpointOptions: To massively increase surface area for nutrient absorption
stages.checkpointExplanation: Villi expand absorptive surface area so digested nutrients pass rapidly into blood.

stages.title: Water Reabsorption in the Large Intestine
stages.narration: Undigested fibre and fluid move into the wider, shorter large intestine where water and essential salts are reclaimed back into the body.
stages.explanation: The large intestine (~1.5 metres long) absorbs remaining water and mineral salts, turning liquid residue into semi-solid waste.
stages.checkpointQuestion: What is the primary role of the large intestine?
checkpointOptions: Absorbing water and some salts from undigested food
stages.checkpointExplanation: The large intestine reclaims water and salts before egestion.

stages.title: Waste Storage & Elimination (Egestion)
stages.narration: Finally, remaining semi-solid waste is stored briefly in the rectum and eliminated from the body through the anus—completing the digestive journey!
stages.explanation: Egestion removes indigestible residue safely from the body, keeping the digestive tract healthy.
stages.checkpointQuestion: What is the biological term for removing undigested solid waste from the body?
stages.checkpointExplanation: Egestion is the final stage of animal nutrition where undigested residue leaves the body.

experientialSimulations.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Science · Ch. 2: Nutrition in Animals

experientialSimulations.subtitle: Adjust Sunlight, CO₂, and Soil Water sliders to watch chloroplast glucose synthesis and live oxygen bubble output change dynamically.
experientialSimulations.instructions: Move the three environmental sliders, observe the limiting factor indicator, and complete the lab checkpoints.

stages.title: Explore Limiting Factors in Leaf Photosynthesis
stages.narration: Increase sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to watch chloroplasts accelerate glucose production and release oxygen bubbles.
stages.explanation: Photosynthesis stops in darkness (0% light) or drought (0% water), demonstrating why all three inputs are essential.
stages.checkpointQuestion: If Sunlight is set to 90% and CO₂ is 80%, what happens to photosynthesis when Water drops to 0%?
checkpointOptions: Photosynthesis stops because water is a limiting raw material
stages.checkpointExplanation: Water is an essential reactant; without it, stomata close and glucose cannot be synthesized.

stages.title: Stomatal Guard Cell Control
stages.narration: When water is plentiful and sunlight shines, guard cells swell and open stomatal pores for CO₂ intake.
stages.explanation: Guard cells protect plants from dehydration by closing stomata during severe water scarcity.
stages.checkpointQuestion: Why do guard cells close stomata during extreme drought?
checkpointOptions: To conserve water by reducing transpiration
stages.checkpointExplanation: Closing stomata prevents excess water vapour loss while conserving leaf hydration.

stages.title: Solar Evaporation to Rainfall Runoff
stages.narration: Sunlight warms oceans and lakes, lifting invisible water vapour high into cooler air where clouds form and rain falls back to land.
stages.explanation: Water is never destroyed in nature—it continuously cycles between liquid, vapour, and ice states.
stages.checkpointQuestion: Which step converts invisible rising water vapour into visible cloud droplets?
stages.checkpointExplanation: Cooling high in the atmosphere condenses vapour back into microscopic liquid droplets.

experientialSimulations.instructions: Close the switch and experiment with Voltage and Resistance sliders to verify I = V / R.

stages.title: Closed Circuit & Electron Flow Control
stages.narration: Close the switch to complete the circuit loop. Watch current rise with higher voltage and drop when resistance increases.
stages.explanation: Ohm’s Law states that Current (I in Amperes) equals Voltage (V) divided by Resistance (R in Ohms).
stages.checkpointQuestion: If Voltage is 12 V and Resistance is 4 Ω in a closed circuit, what current does the ammeter read?
stages.checkpointExplanation: Using I = V / R = 12 V ÷ 4 Ω = 3.0 Amperes.

stages.title: Ingestion & Mechanical Chewing (Mouth)
stages.narration: Digestion begins right in the mouth! Teeth grind food mechanically into a soft bolus while salivary glands mix in saliva.
stages.explanation: Teeth increase surface area by chewing, while salivary amylase starts converting complex starch into simple sugars.
stages.checkpointQuestion: Which nutrient begins chemical digestion right inside the mouth due to saliva?
stages.checkpointExplanation: Salivary amylase breaks starch into simple maltose sugars while chewing.

stages.title: Peristalsis Through the Oesophagus
stages.narration: The chewed bolus enters the food pipe, or oesophagus. Rhythmic muscular waves called peristalsis gently push it downward to the stomach.
stages.explanation: Peristaltic waves push food downward even against gravity; no major chemical digestion occurs here.
stages.checkpointQuestion: What pushes food smoothly down the oesophagus into the stomach?
stages.checkpointExplanation: Rhythmic muscular contractions called peristalsis move food down the alimentary canal.

stages.title: Acid Bath & Churning in the Stomach
stages.narration: Inside the J-shaped stomach, churning mixes food with hydrochloric acid, protective mucus, and protein-digesting enzymes.
stages.explanation: HCl kills harmful bacteria and activates digestive juices to break proteins into simpler compounds, while mucus shields the stomach lining.
stages.checkpointQuestion: What protects the inner lining of the stomach from its own hydrochloric acid?
stages.checkpointExplanation: The stomach secretes mucus that coats and shields its inner wall from acidic damage.

stages.title: Liver Bile & Pancreatic Juices
stages.narration: As chyme enters the upper small intestine, the liver contributes bile stored in the gall bladder and the pancreas adds powerful multi-nutrient enzymes.
stages.explanation: Bile breaks large fat globules into tiny droplets (emulsification), while pancreatic juice acts on carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.
stages.checkpointQuestion: Where is bile produced, and which nutrient does it help break down?
checkpointOptions: Produced in Liver; helps digest Fats
Produced in Large Intestine; absorbs Water
stages.checkpointExplanation: The liver produces bile (stored in the gall bladder) which emulsifies fats.

stages.title: Nutrient Absorption in Small Intestine Villi
stages.narration: Inside the coiled 7.5-metre small intestine, thousands of microscopic finger-like villi absorb glucose, amino acids, and fatty acids directly into the bloodstream!
stages.explanation: Villi multiply internal surface area and contain dense blood capillaries that carry absorbed nutrients to every cell for assimilation.
stages.checkpointQuestion: Why does the inner wall of the small intestine have thousands of finger-like villi?
checkpointOptions: To massively increase surface area for nutrient absorption
stages.checkpointExplanation: Villi expand absorptive surface area so digested nutrients pass rapidly into blood.

stages.title: Water Reabsorption in the Large Intestine
stages.narration: Undigested fibre and fluid move into the wider, shorter large intestine where water and essential salts are reclaimed back into the body.
stages.explanation: The large intestine (~1.5 metres long) absorbs remaining water and mineral salts, turning liquid residue into semi-solid waste.
stages.checkpointQuestion: What is the primary role of the large intestine?
checkpointOptions: Absorbing water and some salts from undigested food
stages.checkpointExplanation: The large intestine reclaims water and salts before egestion.

stages.title: Waste Storage & Elimination (Egestion)
stages.narration: Finally, remaining semi-solid waste is stored briefly in the rectum and eliminated from the body through the anus—completing the digestive journey!
stages.explanation: Egestion removes indigestible residue safely from the body, keeping the digestive tract healthy.
stages.checkpointQuestion: What is the biological term for removing undigested solid waste from the body?
stages.checkpointExplanation: Egestion is the final stage of animal nutrition where undigested residue leaves the body.

experientialSimulations.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Science · Ch. 2: Nutrition in Animals

experientialSimulations.subject: Science
experientialSimulations.learningObjective: Experiment interactively with sunlight, CO₂, and water levels to observe real-time photosynthesis rate, stomata opening, and oxygen bubbles.
experientialSimulations.title: Photosynthesis & Stomata Interactive Virtual Lab
experientialSimulations.subtitle: Adjust Sunlight, CO₂, and Soil Water sliders to watch chloroplast glucose synthesis and live oxygen bubble output change dynamically.
experientialSimulations.instructions: Move the three environmental sliders, observe the limiting factor indicator, and complete the lab checkpoints.

stages.title: Explore Limiting Factors in Leaf Photosynthesis
stages.narration: Increase sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to watch chloroplasts accelerate glucose production and release oxygen bubbles.
stages.explanation: Photosynthesis stops in darkness (0% light) or drought (0% water), demonstrating why all three inputs are essential.
stages.checkpointQuestion: If Sunlight is set to 90% and CO₂ is 80%, what happens to photosynthesis when Water drops to 0%?
checkpointOptions: Photosynthesis stops because water is a limiting raw material
stages.checkpointExplanation: Water is an essential reactant; without it, stomata close and glucose cannot be synthesized.

stages.title: Stomatal Guard Cell Control
stages.narration: When water is plentiful and sunlight shines, guard cells swell and open stomatal pores for CO₂ intake.
stages.explanation: Guard cells protect plants from dehydration by closing stomata during severe water scarcity.
stages.checkpointQuestion: Why do guard cells close stomata during extreme drought?
checkpointOptions: To conserve water by reducing transpiration
stages.checkpointExplanation: Closing stomata prevents excess water vapour loss while conserving leaf hydration.

experientialSimulations.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Science · Ch. 1: Nutrition in Plants

experientialSimulations.subject: Science
experientialSimulations.learningObjective: Simulate how solar temperature changes drive evaporation, cloud condensation, and rainfall across a watershed.
experientialSimulations.title: Interactive Water Cycle & Climate Simulator
experientialSimulations.subtitle: Control solar heat and altitude cooling to watch vapour rise, condense into rain clouds, and flow back to rivers and groundwater.
experientialSimulations.instructions: Adjust the Solar Intensity slider and observe how evaporation, cloud density, and rainfall intensity respond.

stages.title: Solar Evaporation to Rainfall Runoff
stages.narration: Sunlight warms oceans and lakes, lifting invisible water vapour high into cooler air where clouds form and rain falls back to land.
stages.explanation: Water is never destroyed in nature—it continuously cycles between liquid, vapour, and ice states.
stages.checkpointQuestion: Which step converts invisible rising water vapour into visible cloud droplets?
stages.checkpointExplanation: Cooling high in the atmosphere condenses vapour back into microscopic liquid droplets.

experientialSimulations.subject: Science
experientialSimulations.learningObjective: Discover I = V / R experimentally by adjusting battery voltage, resistance, and circuit switch state.
experientialSimulations.title: Electric Circuit & Ohm’s Law Virtual Lab
experientialSimulations.subtitle: Toggle the switch, tune Battery Voltage (V) and Resistance (Ω), and observe live electron flow speed, bulb glow, and Ammeter current.
experientialSimulations.instructions: Close the switch and experiment with Voltage and Resistance sliders to verify I = V / R.

stages.title: Closed Circuit & Electron Flow Control
stages.narration: Close the switch to complete the circuit loop. Watch current rise with higher voltage and drop when resistance increases.
stages.explanation: Ohm’s Law states that Current (I in Amperes) equals Voltage (V) divided by Resistance (R in Ohms).
stages.checkpointQuestion: If Voltage is 12 V and Resistance is 4 Ω in a closed circuit, what current does the ammeter read?
stages.checkpointExplanation: Using I = V / R = 12 V ÷ 4 Ω = 3.0 Amperes.

experientialSimulations.subject: Mathematics
experientialSimulations.learningObjective: Visualize 3D cuboid surface area vs volume and equivalent fractions interactively.
experientialSimulations.title: 3D Geometry, Volume & Interactive Fractions Studio
experientialSimulations.subtitle: Resize 3D cuboid Length, Width, and Height in real time and explore fraction partitioning visually.
experientialSimulations.instructions: Drag the dimension sliders and notice how Volume grows much faster than Surface Area when all sides scale up.

stages.title: Interactive 3D Cuboid & Visual Fraction Bar
stages.narration: Change length, breadth, and height to watch the isometric 3D solid morph while surface area and cubic volume compute live.
stages.explanation: Volume = l × b × h (cubic units); Total Surface Area = 2(lb + bh + hl) (square units).
stages.checkpointQuestion: A cuboid has Length 5 cm, Breadth 4 cm, and Height 3 cm. What is its Volume?
stages.checkpointExplanation: Volume = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 cm³ (while Total Surface Area is 94 cm²).

experientialSimulations.subject: Social Science
experientialSimulations.chapterTitle: Our Changing Earth — Volcanoes & Plate Tectonics
experientialSimulations.learningObjective: Visualize lithospheric plate pressure, magma chamber build-up, and volcanic eruption stages.
experientialSimulations.title: Volcano Cross-Section & Tectonic Stress Simulator
experientialSimulations.subtitle: Increase Mantle Pressure to observe lithospheric plate stress, rising magma in the vent, ash plume formation, and lava flow.
experientialSimulations.instructions: Adjust the Tectonic Pressure slider from Dormant to Active Eruption and inspect all geological layers.

stages.title: Inside an Active Volcano & Plate Boundary
stages.narration: As tectonic plates push together, magma pressure rises inside the mantle chamber until it vents through the crater as glowing lava and ash.
stages.explanation: Crust, Mantle, Magma Chamber, Main Vent, and Crater work together during volcanic activity.
stages.checkpointQuestion: What is the funnel-shaped opening at the top of a volcano where lava and ash emerge?
stages.checkpointExplanation: The crater is the top opening connected to the underground magma chamber via the main vent.

experientialSimulations.sourceReference: HBSE Class 7 Social Science · Ch. 3: Our Changing Earth

experientialSimulations.subject: English
experientialSimulations.learningObjective: Practice tense transformation visually and complete a polite real-world dialogue role-play.
experientialSimulations.title: Visual Tense Timeline & Science Fair Dialogue Role-Play
experientialSimulations.subtitle: Switch sentences across Past, Present, and Future timelines and practice confident spoken responses.
experientialSimulations.instructions: Toggle tenses to see how verbs transform, then pick the most grammatically accurate response in the interactive school role-play.

stages.title: Tense Transformer & Interactive Dialogue
stages.narration: Watch how a single action verb changes across Past, Present, and Future—then speak politely in the school library role-play.
stages.explanation: Choosing the right tense makes storytelling and everyday conversation clear and natural.
stages.checkpointQuestion: Choose the grammatically accurate sentence in Simple Past Tense:
checkpointOptions: Riya built a solar oven yesterday.
Riya builds a solar oven yesterday.
Riya will built a solar oven yesterday.
Riya building a solar oven yesterday.
stages.checkpointExplanation: "Built" is the correct Simple Past form matching the past time marker "yesterday".
